sentences.text: Why don't the electrons in your body just crash into the nucleus?
If an electron got squeezed right next to the nucleus, its position would be super precise.
So its momentum would become hugely uncertain,
meaning it would have wild energy and fly right back out.
The uncertainty principle helps keep atoms from collapsing.
It's part of why you're solid, and not a puddle of sad particles.
Physics: still weird, still holding you together.
